title: Human evolution
group: BIO-EVOL / BIO-ECOL / BIO-PLANT — Evolution, Ecology & Plants
examples: What are the main types of evidence we use to study human evolution?
How did early humans learn to make and use tools?
Can you explain the difference between a fossil and a modern bone?

explain.say: We begin by looking at the fossil record for evidence.

items: When: Early hominids lived millions of years ago
What: Fossils show changes in skull and teeth

explain.say: Another important piece of evidence is the study of skeletal structure.
We also examine dental records to understand diet changes.
Early hominids also left behind evidence of tool use.
In everyday life, understanding tool evolution is very useful.
A common mistake is assuming early humans lived in one place only.

faq.q: What is the difference between a fossil and a modern bone?
faq.a: A fossil is the preserved remains of ancient life, often showing mineralization. A modern bone is bone tissue from a living or recently deceased animal.

faq.q: What does bipedalism mean in human evolution?
faq.a: Bipedalism means walking upright on two legs. This freed the hands for carrying objects and using tools.
asks: Why did we start walking upright?
What is the advantage of walking on two legs?

faq.q: What kind of tools did the earliest hominids use?
faq.a: The earliest tools were simple stone flakes struck from a core stone. These were used for basic cutting and scraping tasks.
asks: Were the first tools made of stone?
What is the simplest tool type?

faq.q: How do scientists know about hominid diets?
faq.a: They study the wear patterns on fossil teeth and look for associated faunal remains. Heavy wear suggests a tougher, more varied diet.
asks: Can teeth tell us what people ate?

faq.q: Did tool use develop suddenly or gradually?
faq.a: The evidence suggests that tool use developed gradually over millions of years. Each new tool type improved upon the last.
asks: Was tool making a sudden invention?
How long did tool use take to develop?

facts: Early hominids were characterized by changes in locomotion, such as bipedalism.
Stone tools, like Oldowan choppers, are among the earliest evidence of human technology.
The fossil record provides evidence of gradual evolutionary changes over millions of years.
Changes in pelvic structure are key evidence supporting upright walking.

quiz.say: What skeletal feature is strongly associated with upright walking in hominids?
quiz.why: A bowl-shaped pelvis supports the weight and mechanics of walking fully upright.

wrong.1: Curved pelvises are more typical of arboreal apes.
wrong.2: Pelvis size alone is not the primary indicator of bipedalism.
wrong.3: While wide, the specific bowl shape is the key adaptation.

quiz.say: Which material was used for the earliest known stone tools?
quiz.why: The initial tools were created by striking flakes off a core stone.

wrong.0: Metal tools represent a much later technological advancement.
wrong.2: Bone tools came later in the evolutionary sequence.
wrong.3: While wood was used, the earliest preserved tools are stone.

quiz.say: If a fossil shows teeth with heavy wear, what does this suggest about the hominid?
quiz.why: Heavy wear suggests the need to process tough, fibrous, or varied food sources.

wrong.1: Soft diets would result in minimal tooth wear.
wrong.2: Water sources do not directly determine tooth wear patterns.
wrong.3: All hominids required a consistent diet for survival.
